class.name: PlayerState
class.brief_description: Per-player data everyone is meant to see: name, id, score, ping.
class.description: A child of the [GameStateBase], not of the [PlayerController], and that is the whole point of the class. A [PlayerController] exists only on the server and on its owning client; a [PlayerState] has to be visible to every peer, so it lives on the node that exists everywhere. Created when a player logs in, from [member GameModeBase.player_state_scene] if one is set. [member player_id] is handed out by the server and is unique for the session - it is what names this player's controller and pawn on every peer, while [member unique_id] is the connection they are on. Extend it in GDScript for anything the scoreboard needs and return the property names from [code]_get_replicated_properties[/code]; the framework keeps them in step with the server's copy.

method.name: _get_replicated_properties
method.description: Override to add your own properties to what is kept in step across peers. Return their names; the framework attaches the synchronizer.

method.name: get_local_role
method.description: What this peer may do with this player state - see [enum World.NetRole].

method.name: get_remote_role
method.description: The mirror image of [method get_local_role]: what the other side may do.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this player state belongs to.

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True on the server, and in a game with no peer at all.

members.member: Whether an [AIController] drives this player rather than a human.
Whether this player is at this machine. Always [code]true[/code] without networking.
Always [code]0[/code] without networking. The field exists so UI written today keeps working once replication fills it in.
Handed out by the server and unique for the session, including for a second player sharing one machine. Controllers and pawns are named after it, so it is how the same player is found on every peer.
Matches [member LocalPlayer.player_index] for a local player.
A general-purpose replicated score. Emits [signal score_changed] when it moves.
Whether this player watches rather than plays. The framework does not act on it; a game mode decides what it means.
The multiplayer peer id once there is networking. [code]1[/code] is the server, which is also what a purely local game reports.

signal.name: player_name_changed
signal.description: The display name changed - on the peer that set it, and on every peer it replicated to.
